target_domain: RoB 2: Randomization Process & Allocation Concealment
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).pdf
directional_bias: Selection Bias (inadequate concealment inflates treatment effect estimates by 15-30% for subjective outcomes)
appraisal_action: Audit whether the allocation sequence was truly random and centrally concealed (e.g. central interactive web/voice randomization or sequentially numbered sealed opaque envelopes) until participant assignment. Evaluate baseline prognostic tables for substantial imbalances between arms that suggest failure of randomization.

target_domain: RoB 2: Deviations from Intended Interventions
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).pdf
appraisal_action: Assess whether participants, carers, and healthcare providers were blinded to intervention allocation. Evaluate if differential non-protocol co-interventions occurred between arms, and verify whether the primary efficacy analysis preserved randomized allocation via an Intention-to-Treat (ITT) population.

target_domain: RoB 2: Missing Outcome Data & Attrition
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).pdf
appraisal_action: Audit whether outcome data were available for all or nearly all randomised participants. If attrition occurred, evaluate whether dropout rates or reasons differed between arms, whether missingness was potentially related to true underlying health status (Missing Not At Random - MNAR), and whether principled sensitivity analyses (e.g. pattern-mixture modeling or multiple imputation) were conducted rather than flawed single imputation like Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF).

target_domain: RoB 2: Measurement of the Outcome
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).pdf
appraisal_action: Evaluate whether outcome assessors were blinded to treatment assignment. For unblinded trials with subjective or investigator-assessed outcomes (such as symptom scores or local radiographic response), flag potential assessment bias. In oncology trials, verify whether progression events were verified by a Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR).

target_domain: RoB 2: Selection of Reported Results
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).pdf
directional_bias: Selective Outcome Reporting Bias (p-hacking / post-hoc endpoint switching)
appraisal_action: Cross-reference reported primary and secondary endpoints, cutoff dates, and statistical sub-analyses against the a priori registered trial protocol (e.g. ClinicalTrials.gov) or published Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) to detect omitted, altered, or post-hoc endpoints.

target_domain: CONSORT Harms 2022: Safety and Toxicity Reporting
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/CONSORT Harms 2022 statement, explanation, and elaboration.pdf
directional_bias: Selective Safety Reporting Bias & Harms Minimization
appraisal_action: Verify that absolute participant counts, percentages, and relative effect sizes (risk ratios or odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals and risk differences) are reported for each primary and secondary harm outcome. Ensure evaluation covers both mild/moderate and severe toxicities without grouping distinct clinical events into broad umbrella categories. Scrutinize any post-randomization patient exclusions under arbitrary 'safety population' definitions.

target_domain: Composite Endpoints: Component Deconstruction & Discordance
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/Users Guides to the Medical Literature.pdf
directional_bias: Dilution of Hard Endpoints (soft components driving overall composite significance)
appraisal_action: When the primary outcome is a composite (e.g. major adverse cardiac events [MACE] or disease-free survival [DFS]), deconstruct the composite into its individual components. Check whether component frequencies and effect estimates are reported separately, and verify whether the overall composite effect is driven primarily by subjective or less critical components (e.g. elective revascularization) while hard endpoints (e.g. all-cause mortality, stroke) show no meaningful difference.

target_domain: CONSORT-PRO: Patient-Reported Outcomes Methodology
source_file: Reference_papers/6.Patient-Reported Outcomes (PROs) & Quality of Life/Reporting of Patient-Reported Outcomes in Randomized Trials.pdf
appraisal_action: Examine whether the PRO instrument is validated in the target population and whether compliance and completion rates over longitudinal follow-up are documented. Audit the pre-specified statistical approach for handling missing PRO data (Item P12a), flagging naive Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF) for informative dropout (MNAR). Enforce a two-tiered MID audit: (1) verify whether observed score differences meet an a priori instrument-specific, anchor-based Minimally Important Difference (MID / MCID); (2) if no anchor-based MID exists, verify whether a validated distribution-based benchmark (e.g. 0.5 SD or 5-10% of scale range) was justified, rather than asserting clinical benefit on statistical significance (p < 0.05) alone.

target_domain: Non-Inferiority: Dual ITT and Per-Protocol Requirement
source_file: Reference_papers/2.Statistics/Interpreting_the_results_of_noninferiority_trials-.pdf
source_item: Cuzick & Sasieni Section: ITT and Per-Protocol Analyses
directional_bias: Bias Toward Equivalence (non-adherence in ITT dilutes treatment contrasts, artificially favoring non-inferiority)
appraisal_action: Enforce mandatory reporting and concordance of BOTH Per-Protocol (PP) and Intention-to-Treat (ITT) populations. In non-inferiority trials, non-compliance, cross-overs, and dropouts bias results toward the null, making dissimilar treatments look deceptively equivalent. If non-inferiority is demonstrated only in the ITT population but fails or is omitted in the PP population, the non-inferiority claim must be challenged.

target_domain: Non-Inferiority: Margin Selection & Retention of Control Efficacy
source_file: Reference_papers/2.Statistics/Non-inferiority Trials in cardiology.pdf
source_item: Section on Determining Delta Margins and M1/M2
appraisal_action: Audit the pre-specified non-inferiority margin (Delta). Verify whether the margin was justified statistically and clinically based on historical superiority data of the active comparator against placebo. Confirm that the confidence interval excludes Delta, thereby preserving at least 50% (M1/2) of the active control's established historical efficacy.

target_domain: Non-Inferiority: Assay Sensitivity & Active Control Constancy
source_file: Reference_papers/2.Statistics/Tools & Techniques - Statistics- Non-inferiority trials.pdf
source_item: Section: Constancy Assumption and Assay Sensitivity
directional_bias: Constancy Assumption Violation (underperforming control falsely validates test drug)
appraisal_action: Evaluate whether the trial demonstrated assay sensitivity by establishing that the active control performed consistently with historical reference trials in the same patient population, dosing regimen, and concomitant therapies. If active control efficacy was markedly diminished, non-inferiority between arms does not demonstrate therapeutic efficacy.

target_domain: Oncology Endpoints: Overall Survival Dilution via Post-Progression Crossover
source_file: Reference_papers/3.Oncology Endpoints & Trial Design/Approaches to Assessment of Overall Survival in Oncology Clinical Trials.pdf
source_item: Section on Treatment Switching and Crossover Adjustment
directional_bias: Dilution Bias (underestimating true OS hazard ratio of experimental therapy)
appraisal_action: Assess whether control arm patients crossed over to the experimental agent or received active subsequent lines upon disease progression. Evaluate whether statistical adjustment models for treatment switching (such as Rank-Preserving Structural Failure Time [RPSFT] or two-stage estimation) were reported alongside naive ITT analyses to account for OS dilution.

target_domain: Clinical Trial Endpoints: Surrogate vs Hard Clinical Outcome Dissociation
source_file: Reference_papers/3.Oncology Endpoints & Trial Design/Approaches to Assessment of Overall Survival in Oncology Clinical Trials.pdf
source_item: Section on Surrogate Endpoints and Accelerated Approval
directional_bias: Surrogate Invalidation Bias (intermediate marker gains failing to translate into hard survival or functional benefits)
appraisal_action: Examine whether statistically significant gains in intermediate surrogate endpoints (such as PFS/ORR in oncology, LDL-C/blood pressure in cardiology, eGFR decline in nephrology, or HbA1c in diabetology) translate into demonstrable hard clinical outcomes (overall survival, reduced irreversible organ failure, or verified health-related quality of life). Explicitly audit potential dissociation between surrogate improvements and patient-centered clinical endpoints.

target_domain: Immune Response: iRECIST Confirmation & Pseudoprogression
source_file: Reference_papers/3.Oncology Endpoints & Trial Design/iRECIST guidelines for response criteria for use in trials testing immunotherapeutics.pdf
source_item: Section on Confirmation of Progression (iUPD to iCPD)
directional_bias: Pseudoprogression Misclassification Bias (premature cessation of efficacious immunotherapy)
appraisal_action: In checkpoint inhibitor trials, verify whether initial tumor enlargement was categorized as unconfirmed progressive disease (iUPD). Confirm that the protocol mandated repeat imaging 4 to 8 weeks later to confirm true progression (iCPD) before patient discontinuation, guarding against premature drug withdrawal caused by transient immune-cell infiltration.

target_domain: Survival Statistics: Proportional Hazards Assumption in Cox Models
source_file: Reference_papers/2.Statistics/Survival probabilities (the Kaplan-Meier method).pdf
source_item: Section on Assumptions and Cox Proportional Hazards
directional_bias: Model Misspecification Bias (inaccurate summary Hazard Ratio when hazards are non-proportional)
appraisal_action: Inspect Kaplan-Meier survival curves for crossing curves, delayed separation, or converging tails. Such patterns violate the proportional hazards assumption of the Cox model, rendering a single constant Hazard Ratio (HR) misleading. Audit the text for formal tests of proportional hazards (e.g. Schoenfeld residuals) or non-proportional alternatives (such as restricted mean survival time [RMST] or milestone survival rates). If the manuscript is silent on proportional hazards testing, document this as an unverified methodological assumption requiring clinician visual inspection of the survival curves.

target_domain: Statistical Multiplicity: Subgroup Claims & Multiplicity Correction
source_file: Reference_papers/2.Statistics/Multiple significance tests the Bonferroni method.pdf
source_item: Section on Subgroup Analyses and Multiplicity
directional_bias: Type I Error Inflation (False Positive Subgroup Claims via Data Dredging)
appraisal_action: Audit any claims of differential treatment benefit in subgroup strata. Demand a formal statistical test for interaction (p-interaction) rather than relying on within-group p-values. Downgrade any subgroup findings that were post-hoc, underpowered, or lacked adjustment for multiple hypothesis testing.

target_domain: PRISMA 2020: Search Strategy & Study Selection Flow
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/PRISMA 2020 explanation and elaboration updated guidance and exemplars for reporting systematic reviews.pdf
appraisal_action: Verify whether complete, reproducible search strings across multiple medical bibliographic databases (e.g. MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL) are provided, including date limits and search filters. Audit the PRISMA flow diagram for accounting of all identified records, screened titles/abstracts, full texts retrieved, and specific reasons for excluded studies.

target_domain: PRISMA 2020: Statistical Heterogeneity & Pooling Model Choice
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/PRISMA 2020 explanation and elaboration updated guidance and exemplars for reporting systematic reviews.pdf
directional_bias: Inappropriate Data Pooling Bias (falsely narrow confidence intervals via fixed-effect models)
appraisal_action: Evaluate reporting of Cochran's Q test and Higgins I^2 statistic. When substantial between-study statistical or clinical heterogeneity is present, fixed-effect model pooling is methodologically unsound and underestimates uncertainty. Check whether sources of heterogeneity were formally investigated through pre-specified subgroup analyses or meta-regression.

target_domain: PRISMA 2020: Small Study Effects & Publication Bias Direction
source_file: Reference_papers/2.Statistics/The effect of publication bias magnitude and direction.pdf
source_item: Section: Modeling Publication Bias Magnitude and Direction
directional_bias: Dissemination Bias (selective publication inflating pooled effect sizes)
appraisal_action: Assess whether publication bias and small-study effects were evaluated. Restrict formal statistical asymmetry tests (e.g. Egger linear regression or Begg rank correlation) to meta-analyses with at least 10 included trials (k >= 10) to avoid false-positive or underpowered conclusions. Evaluate the likely direction and magnitude of bias on the summary estimate before downgrading evidence certainty, acknowledging that unpublished small trials do not universally alter the clinical bottom line.

target_domain: Meta-Analysis: Pooled Effect Significance vs Individual Study Power
source_file: Reference_papers/2.Statistics/Meta-analysis- Its strengths and limitations.pdf
source_item: Section: Statistical Power, Aggregation, and Fragility
appraisal_action: Audit whether the summary meta-analytic effect reaches statistical significance primarily by aggregating multiple small, individually underpowered trials with high risk of bias. Examine leave-one-out sensitivity analyses to verify that the pooled result is not fragile or reliant upon a single dominant study.

target_domain: GRADE: Quality and Certainty of Evidence Across Outcomes
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/GRADE handbook.pdf
appraisal_action: Verify whether a Summary of Findings (SoF) table presents GRADE certainty ratings (High, Moderate, Low, Very Low) for each critical patient-important outcome. Audit the five systematic downgrade domains: risk of bias, inconsistency of results, indirectness of evidence, imprecision of effect estimates, and publication bias.

target_domain: STROBE: Confounder Selection & Multivariable Adjustment
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) Explanation and Elaboration.pdf
appraisal_action: Audit whether key prognostic confounders were identified a priori using causal diagrams or clinical rationale, rather than data-driven stepwise selection. Verify whether appropriate statistical adjustment (e.g. multivariable regression, propensity score matching, or inverse probability weighting) was performed, and assess whether sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounding (such as E-values) were reported.

target_domain: STROBE: Cohort Selection Bias & Reverse Causality
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) Explanation and Elaboration.pdf
appraisal_action: Assess whether cohort eligibility criteria created survival selection (e.g. excluding individuals who died prior to a landmark age or cohort entry). Check whether baseline exposure or biomarker measurement timing could reflect subclinical, pre-existing disease processes, thereby causing reverse causality.

target_domain: RECORD: Routinely Collected Healthcare & Claims Data
source_file: Reference_papers/5.Real-World Evidence & Health Economics/The REporting of studies Conducted using Observational Routinely-collected health Data (RECORD) Statement.pdf
appraisal_action: Verify whether validated diagnostic and procedural coding algorithms (e.g. ICD-9/10, CPT) were used to define exposures, outcomes, and comorbidities. Audit data linkage quality, registry completeness, and handling of out-of-system clinical events and missing administrative fields.

target_domain: Pharmacoepidemiology: Immortal Time Bias
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) Explanation and Elaboration.pdf
directional_bias: Immortal Time Bias (spuriously inflating survival in treated or exposed cohorts)
appraisal_action: Verify whether the interval between cohort entry and start of intervention was misclassified as exposed follow-up time. Demand time-dependent exposure modeling or landmark analysis to ensure participants could not accumulate immortal survival time prior to treatment initiation.

target_domain: STARD 2015: Diagnostic Reference Standard & Blinding
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/STARD 2015 - diagnostic accuracy.pdf
directional_bias: Observer / Review Bias (knowledge of one test influencing interpretation of the other)
appraisal_action: Audit whether the index test and the reference standard are defined in sufficient technical detail to allow clinical replication. Verify whether readers of the index test were blinded to the reference standard results and clinical history, and whether interpreters of the reference standard were blinded to index test findings.

target_domain: STARD 2015: Verification Bias (Work-up Bias)
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/STARD 2015 - diagnostic accuracy.pdf
directional_bias: Partial / Differential Verification Bias (inflating diagnostic sensitivity and distorting specificity)
appraisal_action: Examine whether all enrolled participants received verification with the gold reference standard regardless of their index test result. If patients with negative index tests were less likely to undergo reference standard assessment (partial verification), verify whether appropriate statistical corrections or clinical follow-up were conducted.

target_domain: STARD 2015: Spectrum Bias & Case-Mix Representativeness
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/STARD 2015 - diagnostic accuracy.pdf
appraisal_action: Assess whether the study cohort reflects the full clinical spectrum of presenting suspect patients in real-world clinical practice (including mild disease, early stages, and competing alternative diagnoses) rather than an artificial two-gate design comparing severely diseased cases against completely healthy controls.

target_domain: SPIRIT 2013: Sample Size Calculation Assumptions
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/SPIRIT 2013 Statement Defining Standard Protocol Items for Clinical Trials.pdf
appraisal_action: Audit the statistical assumptions underlying the sample size calculation: expected control event rate, targeted minimum clinically meaningful effect size, alpha level, statistical power, and anticipated loss to follow-up. Challenge protocols where optimistic effect size assumptions yield inadequate power for realistic therapeutic gains.

target_domain: SPIRIT 2013: Pre-Specified Statistical Analysis Plan
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/SPIRIT 2013 Statement Defining Standard Protocol Items for Clinical Trials.pdf
appraisal_action: Verify whether the protocol specifies primary and secondary statistical models, analysis population definitions (e.g. ITT vs modified ITT), handling of missing data, and explicit plans for subgroup or adjusted analyses prior to participant enrollment or unblinding.

target_domain: SPIRIT 2013: Interim Analyses & Trial Stopping Rules
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/SPIRIT 2013 Statement Defining Standard Protocol Items for Clinical Trials.pdf
directional_bias: Multiplicity Inflation & Premature Trial Termination Bias
appraisal_action: Audit the description of planned interim analyses, including pre-specified stopping guidelines for efficacy, futility, or safety harms. Ensure that an appropriate alpha-spending method is defined and that governance oversight (e.g. an independent Data Safety Monitoring Board [DSMB]) is established.

target_domain: CHEERS 2022: Time Horizon & Discounting Rationale
source_file: Reference_papers/5.Real-World Evidence & Health Economics/Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) statement updated reporting guidance for health economic evaluations.pdf
appraisal_action: Verify whether the chosen analytic time horizon adequately reflects the long-term clinical and cost trajectories of the disease state. Confirm that annual discount rates applied to costs and health outcomes are explicitly reported alongside an evidence-based justification for the selected rate.

target_domain: CHEERS 2022: Decision Model Structure & Uncertainty Analysis
source_file: Reference_papers/5.Real-World Evidence & Health Economics/Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) statement updated reporting guidance for health economic evaluations.pdf
directional_bias: Model Structural Bias & Parameter Uncertainty Underestimation
appraisal_action: Audit the economic decision model structure (e.g. Markov cohort, decision tree, microsimulation) for clinical validity of health states and transition assumptions. Check whether comprehensive parameter and structural uncertainty were evaluated using both deterministic sensitivity analysis (tornado diagrams) and probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA with cost-effectiveness acceptability curves).

target_domain: CHEERS 2022: Health State Utility & QALY Measurement
source_file: Reference_papers/5.Real-World Evidence & Health Economics/Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) statement updated reporting guidance for health economic evaluations.pdf
appraisal_action: Evaluate the instruments and methodologies used to derive health state utility weights (e.g. EQ-5D, HUI, time trade-off). Audit whether value sets reflect the appropriate jurisdictional population and whether decrement assumptions for treatment toxicities and disease progression are clinically substantiated.

target_domain: SANRA: Narrative Review Quality Domains
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/SANRA—a scale for the quality assessment of narrative review articles.pdf
appraisal_action: Evaluate the 6 SANRA quality domains: (1) justification of topic importance, (2) statement of concrete aims, (3) description of the literature search methodology, (4) referencing consistency, (5) scientific reasoning and balanced evidence synthesis, and (6) appropriate presentation of outcome data. Explicitly note that narrative assertions cannot replace systematic quantitative pooling for evaluating therapeutic efficacy.

target_domain: REMARK: Biospecimen Handling & Assay Pre-Analytics
source_file: Reference_papers/4.Biomarker & Genomic Medicine/Reporting Recommendations for Tumor Marker Prognostic Studies (REMARK) Explanation and Elaboration.pdf
appraisal_action: Audit reporting of biospecimen collection, handling, processing, and preservation methods (e.g. cold ischemia time, fixative type). Verify that the laboratory assay, antibody clones, primers, scoring protocols, and limits of detection are described with sufficient detail and reproducibility metrics to enable independent replication.

target_domain: REMARK: Cut-point Pre-Specification & Overfitting
source_file: Reference_papers/4.Biomarker & Genomic Medicine/Reporting Recommendations for Tumor Marker Prognostic Studies (REMARK) Explanation and Elaboration.pdf
directional_bias: Optimism Bias & Type I Error Inflation
appraisal_action: Examine how biomarker positivity cut-points were determined. If continuous biomarker variables were categorized into binary groups using data-dependent 'optimal' cutpoint searching (minimum p-value method) without independent validation in a separate holdout cohort, effect sizes and p-values are heavily overfitted.

target_domain: REMARK: Independent Prognostic Value & Predictive Distinction
source_file: Reference_papers/4.Biomarker & Genomic Medicine/Reporting Recommendations for Tumor Marker Prognostic Studies (REMARK) Explanation and Elaboration.pdf
appraisal_action: Verify whether multivariable survival models evaluate whether the biomarker contributes incremental prognostic information beyond established standard clinical and pathological staging variables. Explicitly audit whether the study distinguishes a purely prognostic biomarker from a predictive biomarker (which strictly requires demonstrating a significant treatment-by-biomarker interaction test in a randomized trial).

target_domain: Genomic Medicine: ctDNA Liquid Biopsy Technical Limits & CHIP
source_file: Reference_papers/4.Biomarker & Genomic Medicine/Circulating Tumor DNA A Pan-Cancer Biomarker in Solid Tumors with Prognostic and Predictive Value.pdf
source_item: Section: Biological and Technical Challenges of ctDNA Detection
appraisal_action: Audit assay Limit of Detection (LOD) and Variant Allele Fraction (VAF%). Classify the ctDNA Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) assay architecture: explicitly document whether it is 'tumor-informed' (bespoke patient-specific variant panel, high analytical sensitivity LOD <= 0.01% VAF) or 'tumor-naïve' (fixed plasma-only hotspot panel, carrying higher false-negative rates for low-shedding microscopic residual disease). Verify whether matched peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) sequencing was conducted to exclude Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) mutations.

target_domain: Survey Research: Sampling Strategy & Target Population Representativeness
source_file: Reference_papers/Good practice in the conduct and reporting of survey research, International Journal for Quality in Health CareS.pdf
appraisal_action: Assess the definition of the target population and the sampling frame. Audit whether probability-based random sampling or convenience sampling was utilized, and evaluate whether exclusions or coverage errors systematically underrepresented key demographic or clinical subgroups.

target_domain: Survey Research: Response Rate & Non-Response Bias
source_file: Reference_papers/Good practice in the conduct and reporting of survey research, International Journal for Quality in Health CareS.pdf
appraisal_action: Verify that the response rate calculation is explicitly reported, accounting for undeliverable questionnaires and ineligible respondents. Evaluate whether non-response bias was assessed (e.g. through comparison of early vs late responders or comparing respondent characteristics to known target population demographics).

target_domain: Survey Research: Questionnaire Design & Psychometric Validity
source_file: Reference_papers/Good practice in the conduct and reporting of survey research, International Journal for Quality in Health CareS.pdf
appraisal_action: Examine whether the survey questions utilized previously validated psychometric scales or underwent formal cognitive pre-testing and pilot testing. Audit item clarity, neutral framing, avoidance of leading or double-barreled questions, and internal consistency reliability.

target_domain: CONSORT Harms 2022: Omitted Harms Rationale & Zero-Event Disclosure
source_file: Reference_papers/1.Foundational/Core 10/CONSORT Harms 2022 statement, explanation, and elaboration.pdf
appraisal_action: Verify that when assessed harm outcomes lack presented effect estimates, an explicit scientific rationale and repository data-access link are provided (Item 17a2). Audit whether prespecified harm outcomes that yielded zero occurrences are explicitly declared (Item 17c) rather than silently omitted from the results.

target_domain: Non-Inferiority: Strategic Objective (Alternative vs Replacement) & Margin Calibration
source_file: Reference_papers/2.Statistics/Exploring_different_objectives_in_non-inferiority_.pdf
directional_bias: Unjustified Efficacy Sacrifice (accepting inferior efficacy without compensating secondary benefit)
appraisal_action: Audit the strategic objective of the non-inferiority trial. If designed as a 'replacement' intervention (promising improved safety, tolerability, convenience, or cost), verify that the non-inferiority margin (Delta) is clinically calibrated to and outweighed by the demonstrated secondary benefit. If designed purely as an 'alternative' option with no secondary advantages, challenge any margin that permits meaningful loss of efficacy.

target_domain: CHEERS 2022: Analysis Plan, Distributional Equity & Patient Involvement
source_file: Reference_papers/5.Real-World Evidence & Health Economics/Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) statement updated reporting guidance for health economic evaluations.pdf
appraisal_action: Audit whether an a priori Health Economic Analysis Plan (HEAP) was registered (Item 4). Verify whether distributional cost-effectiveness and equity impacts across patient subgroups were assessed (Item 19). Audit reporting of patient and public involvement (PPIE) in study conceptualization and interpretation (Items 21 & 25). For pre-2022 evaluations, document absence as an evolving reporting limitation rather than an invalidating flaw.
